title: Task Dependency Critical Path Scheduler
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: A vis-network dependency graph of nine illustrative tasks from an ADC research project, with durations in hours. The learner answers five questions in a fixed order, one attempt each: the earliest finish of T5, the tasks on the critical path, the slack of T4, the project duration, and the new project duration after T3 is reduced from 3 hours to 1 hour. After each answer the sim shows the correct answer, the reason, and the forward pass of earliest start and finish times; after question 5 a T3 duration slider shows how the critical path moves. The final score is reported as n of 5 correct with a mastery threshold of 4.

educational.topic: Task dependencies, critical path, and slack in an agent team's work breakdown
learningObjectives: Calculate the earliest finish time, the critical path, and the slack of tasks in a nine-task dependency graph, and recalculate the project duration after one duration changes, with at least 4 of 5 answers correct

accessibility.notes: The graph has an aria-label listing every task, duration, and dependency. All scored input uses native controls reachable with the Tab key: a text box (Enter submits), T1 to T9 toggle buttons with aria-pressed, a range slider, and a select for task details. Critical tasks carry a star and the word critical plus a thick border; tasks in the current answer carry a triangle and a dashed border; colors are from the Okabe-Ito blue/orange palette. Mouse-wheel zoom and drag-to-pan are disabled so the iframe never captures page scrolling.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked forward-pass practice: the learner commits a calculation before the sim reveals the answer, the reason, and the forward pass on the graph, then explores how changing one duration moves the critical path
keyQuestions: Which chain of tasks sets the project duration?
How much can a task slip without delaying the project?
Why does cutting 2 hours from a critical task save only 1 hour?
commonMisconceptions: The project duration is the sum of all task durations
Shortening a critical task always shortens the project by the same amount
assessmentOpportunities: Score on the single attempt for each of five questions; mastery is at least 4 of 5 correct
Find the value of T3 at which the critical path switches between the T3 and T4 branches
Explain in one sentence why cutting 2 hours from T3 saved only 1 hour

controls.name: Answer (hours)
controls.purpose: Enter a number of hours for questions 1, 3, 4, and 5; Enter submits

controls.name: T1 to T9
controls.purpose: Select the tasks on the critical path for question 2

controls.name: Submit
controls.purpose: Commit the answer; one attempt per question; a non-number is not counted as an attempt

controls.name: Next question
controls.purpose: Advance to the next question after the current one has been answered

controls.name: T3 duration
controls.purpose: After question 5, change T3 from 1 to 6 hours and watch the project duration and critical path update (exploration, not scored)

controls.name: Restart
controls.purpose: Clear all answers and return to the starting state with no times shown

controls.name: Read a task
controls.purpose: Show a task's duration, prerequisites, and any times already revealed (exploration, not scored)
